properties.digitized_from: Pier 70 Design for Development, Figure 6.4.2 - Maximum Building Height (p.155).
properties.digitization_method: REDONE 2026-09-14: the previous version of this polygon was traced using a transform fit from 5 street intersections plus Historic Building 12's real footprint as a 6th anchor. A user-flagged visual comparison against satellite imagery showed the resulting blocks were systematically rotated/sheared (~13-14 degrees off, and not even mutually orthogonal) relative to the real street grid -- confirmed by comparing traced block bearings against the real, independently-surveyed Building 14 footprint (DataSF Building Footprints, blklot 4052001), which sits at the real street grid's true orientation (~356/86 degrees, consistent with SF's known ~4-degree grid skew). Root cause: an error in the original corner-correspondence matching, not a diagram-scan distortion. REBUILT using a fresh 6-point affine transform: 5 real street-intersection control points (20th St x Illinois St, 20th St x Michigan St, 21st St x Illinois St, 21st St x Michigan St, 22nd St x Illinois St -- fetched from OpenStreetMap via this project's own src/fetch_streets.py) plus the real, independently-confirmed centroid of Historic Building 12's own Assessor parcel (blklot 4114010) as a 6th, spatially-distant anchor. This fit has a residual error of 1-8m against its own 6 control points (far tighter than the previous transform), AND was validated by checking that it reproduces the correct real-world bearing (independently confirmed via Building 14's footprint) rather than just checking point-position error, which is what let the previous version's shear go undetected. Pixel corners for this block were re-read directly from Figure 6.4.2 with fresh, fine-grained crops. Residual error against the 6 control points is roughly 1-8m; treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m given the additional (small) error from reading this specific block's own corners off the diagram. CORRECTED 2026-09-16 (Pier 70 systematic feature-by-feature pass): user-flagged visual check found this block's traced box was far too narrow -- only ~57px/40m wide against the diagram's real ~125px/95m width, sitting entirely inside the true box rather than matching its edges. Re-measured programmatically instead of by eye: isolated this legend color (RGB [128,193,219]) in a fresh crop, confirmed a clean rectangle (no trapezoid) at pixel x 962-1075, y 984-1206 (spanning both of this block's own internal sub-division cells, visible as a thin gray divider line partway down that is not a real boundary), and converted via the same validated 6-point affine transform. New area (~0.59 acres) is roughly 2.4x the previous (wrong) trace. RESOLVED 2026-09-16 (same day, full geometry restart): the 'Pier 70 Building 2 (Warehouse No. 2)' overlap mentioned below no longer applies -- Building 2 was found to be badly mislocated and has been relocated to its real east-cluster position next to Buildings 12 and 21 (see that file); it no longer overlaps this parcel. Also created a small (122 m2) new overlap with Parcel C1 -- these two are adjacent planned parcels that should meet cleanly (unlike the Building 2 case), so clipped against C1's own committed geometry via shapely difference(). CORRECTED 2026-09-17 (found while checking Irish Hill Playground's request to touch C2's western edge -- unrelated to the separate 21st-St-row investigation happening the same day): this block's previously-committed geometry did not match Figure 6.4.2's own blue 'Residential' fill at all -- color-region detection (isolating RGB [128,193,219], the same color used for C1) found this block's true fill is a clean rectangle at pixel (891,912)-(995,1117), extending roughly 70px (~20m) further WEST and starting further north than the previously-committed shape. Confirmed this is a distinct connected component from C1's own fill (C1 occupies y~776-887, a separate blob, with a real ~25px gap between them). Converted via the same validated 6-point affine transform. Verified 0 overlap with C1. REPOSITIONED 2026-09-17 (user override: 'take my input as override... turn that Michigan span into 21st st and adjust parcel positioning accordingly'): re-anchored to the corrected planned 21st St line (see pier70_21st_street.geojson -- built from Michigan St's own real terminus point, perpendicular to Illinois/Louisiana's real ~175.5-degree bearing), replacing the Figure 6.4.2 pixel-traced position used previously. Shifted by the same amount as the nearest point on the repositioned C1 (interpolated between C1's own west/east corner shifts by longitude) to preserve their existing adjacency (previously confirmed touching within normal trace precision) -- own shape/size unchanged. Resulting gap to the repositioned C1 is 7.9m, slightly wider than before but still within this project's normal trace tolerance. EXTENDED 2026-09-17 (user-flagged: should border 22nd St like HDY1/2): south corners (SW/SE) extended straight down to the real 22nd St curb line at each corner's own longitude, using the same 9.8m offset (6.8m curb + ~3m sidewalk allowance) as HDY1/2's own 22nd St edge, rather than the bare 6.8m curb (which the user separately flagged as encroaching on the sidewalk). North/east/west edges unchanged. Area grows accordingly. EXTENDED 2026-09-17 (user-flagged: should border Louisiana St, same as C1): east edge (NE/SE) extended to real Louisiana St at each corner's own latitude, same 9.8m offset. Area grows from ~2,052 to ~5,785 sq m. CORRECTED 2026-09-17 (user-flagged, second time: 'HDY1/2 and C2 still eat away at the sidewalk on the south side'): back-calculated this block's actual achieved offset from the real 22nd St centerline at its SE corner and found only ~4.4m, not the documented/intended 9.8m -- a genuine bug in how that corner was computed in the prior pass (its NE and SW corners, computed the same way, checked out correctly at the intended offset; only the SE corner, which needs to satisfy the 22nd-St-offset AND Louisiana-St-offset constraints simultaneously since it's a dual-street corner, was wrong -- the prior pass appears to have only applied one of the two constraints). Recomputed by iterating both constraints to convergence (offset 9.8m north of real 22nd St's centerline at a trial longitude, then 9.8m west of real Louisiana St's centerline at the resulting latitude, repeating until stable): corner moves from (-122.38486454324594, 37.758227958827085) to (-122.3848693714351, 37.75827576653485), a ~5.4m shift, now correctly clearing the sidewalk on both frontages. ADJUSTED 2026-09-17 (user-flagged, third time: 'HDY1/2 and C2 south border should align with sidewalk south side'): direct satellite comparison (src/satellite_check.py, reference lines at 6.8m/9.8m/13m/18.8m offsets from the real 22nd St centerline across the whole Illinois-to-Louisiana frontage) found that HDY1/2's own hand-drawn south corner (nearest this block, on the other side of the small gap between them) sits at 18.8m off the centerline, not 9.8m -- and 18.8m matches the visible sidewalk/lot boundary better across this whole frontage than the 9.8m formula this project had been using. Recomputed both south corners at 18.8m instead of 9.8m: SW corner (only constrained by 22nd St) moved directly; SE corner (dual-constrained by 22nd St AND Louisiana St, since it's the corner where both meet) recomputed by iterating both constraints to convergence at the new 18.8m 22nd-St offset (Louisiana's own 9.8m offset, unrelated to the sidewalk question, is unchanged). This aligns this block's south edge with HDY1/2's, satisfying the user's request that the two blocks' south borders read as one consistent line. Area shrinks from ~5,785 to ~4,991 sq m.
properties.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- this block is not yet built and does not correspond to any subdivided Assessor parcel: it currently sits on vacant/graded land, surface parking, or an existing industrial building slated for demolition within Brookfield's 28-acre district (unaddressed in DataSF's Assessor roll). Redone 2026-09-14 with a corrected, shear-free transform (see digitization_method) -- treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m, not survey-grade. NOTE: this polygon is NOT clipped against real streets or existing buildings -- unlike Potrero's approximate blocks, several of Pier 70's D4D blocks are sited on existing industrial buildings that will be demolished, so overlap with a currently-real building is often expected, not an error; a boundary that appears to touch or slightly cross a street centerline reflects this transform's 1-8m residual error, not a deliberate encroachment. RESOLVED 2026-09-16: no longer overlaps 'Pier 70 Building 2 (Warehouse No. 2)' -- that file's placement was corrected to its real position elsewhere on the site (see that file's digitization_method). CORRECTED 2026-09-17: re-measured directly from Figure 6.4.2's own color fill, replacing a previously wrong position -- see digitization_method.
properties.why_no_real_parcel: A real Assessor parcel may exist under this block (part of Brookfield's larger, largely unaddressed 28-acre site), but it has not been subdivided per the masterplan's individual named parcels -- this uses hand-traced approximate geometry instead.
properties.regulatory_context: Residential, 90 ft max per Figure 6.4.2. C2A, a sub-portion of this parcel, is one of two 100%-affordable parcels in this cluster per a 2020 Port Commission resolution (the other is C1B, part of Parcel C1). No construction-start source found.
properties.notes: Approximate polygon for a real, D4D-adopted parcel -- see accuracy_caveat.
